title: Traffic Shepherd Playbook and Release Digest — Apr 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose and framing:
This playbook introduces the 'Traffic Shepherd' approach for gradual traffic shifts and post-deploy digest notes. It's intended for medium-complexity releases (multi-region, multi-model routing) where we need fine-grained control over flow rate, quick detection of quality regressions, and automated rollback triggers.

Scope and when to use:
- Use this for feature or infra releases where traffic can be split by header/route (not for DB schema-only changes).
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated clusters with regional routing.
- Not required for small config-only flips (<1% user impact).

High-level phases (quick):
1) Preflight & dry-run (T-72h → T-12h)
2) Canary shepherding (T-1h → +24h)
3) Controlled ramp and steady state (+1d → +7d)
4) Digest, retro, and postmortem (day 7 → day 21)

Preflight checklist (owner: release lead):
- [ ] Confirm release branch merged and CI green. Add PR link to release chat.
- [ ] Verify artifact hashes stored in release tag.
- [ ] Update canary config: initial weight, step increments, max duration.
- [ ] Run dry-run traffic on staging with sample KV cache to validate latencies (runbook step ID: TS-DRY-01).
- [ ] Sanity-run smoke tests: generation, chat streaming, embeddings batch.
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards exist and show baseline for the last 14 days.
- [ ] Ensure alert rotations staffed: release lead, on-call SRE, owner for model.
- [ ] Lock downstream change windows (data pipelines, telemetry exporters).
- [ ] Post preflight summary in SLACK:#release-ops with timestamp and checklist link.

Canary shepherding plan (owner: canary shepherd):
- Shepherding principles: small steps, validate both infra and quality, maintain knot points for quick reversal.
- Starting weight: 0.5% traffic to new variant (config: router.weight=0.005).
- Step increments: 0.5% → 1% → 2% → 5% → 10% (every 30–60 minutes after confirmation).
- Max observation window per step: 30 minutes (extend to 60 if any borderline signals).
- Maximum parallel canaries per region: 1 active at a time (stagger regions by 15 minutes).

Step validation checklist (per increment):
- [ ] Success criteria: 95th pct latency <= baseline + 30ms AND error rate delta < 0.2 percentage points.
- [ ] Quality check: automated prompt sample set (internal set ID: TS_PROMPTS_v3) should have QA pass-rate >= 98%.
- [ ] Rate-limited sampling of user queries for manual inspection (security redaction in place).
- [ ] No new 5xx patterns in trace sampling and no sustained increase in tail latency.
- [ ] Confirm KV cache warmup behavior within expected window (see caching-runbook#kv-warmup).
- [ ] If any failure, immediately revert weight to last known-good percentage and escalate.

Automated guards and rollback criteria:
- Auto-revert triggers (automated, immediate):
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m rolling window OR 
  - p95 latency > baseline + 100ms for 5m OR
  - Runtime OOMs or node terminations detected in cluster for 2m
- Manual rollback triggers (investigate before revert):
  - Quality regression detected by prompt set (pass-rate drop >= 2.5%)
  - Customer-facing SLA degrade flagged by SRE or CS
- Revert plan: revert router config -> scale down variant -> deploy hotfix branch if needed. Document revert step in Slack thread.

Rollout calendar (example timeline for a weekday release):
- T-72h: Draft release notes, collect linked PRs, assign owners.
- T-48h: Preflight complete, telemetry baseline capture.
- T-24h: Dry-run verification in staging; notify CS and allies.
- T-4h: Final CI/infra checks, freeze non-critical merges.
- T-1h: Start canary at 0.5% region A.
- T0+30m: If OK, bump to 1% region A.
- T0+1.5h: If OK, bump to 2% region A; start 0.5% in region B.
- T0+3h: Ramp to 5% region A, 2% region B; open post-deploy monitoring channel.
- T0+8h: Target 10% across regions (if stable).
- Day 1–3: Continue slow ramp to desired overall percentage, enable additional variants if part of rollout.

Communication plan (who says what):
- Release lead: periodic updates every step in SLACK:#release-ops and ticket comments.
- SRE on-call: initial acceptance and immediate incident lead if auto-guard trips.
- Product PM: send initial 'Release started' email to stakeholders when first canary begins.
- Support rotation: brief CS on expected behavioral changes + canned troubleshooting steps.

Post-release digest template (fill in day 1 and day 7):
- Release tag: <git-tag>
- Owner(s): <owner list>
- Regions impacted: <regions>
- Traffic curve summary: initial → final weights per region
- Telemetry highlights: latency, errors, throughput deltas vs baseline
- Notable anomalies: traces, 5xx spike, OOMs, cache warmup issues
- Customer impact: any escalations, reported incidents
- Rollbacks: any reverts performed (time, reason, mitigation)
- Follow-ups & action items: owners and target dates

Postmortem / retro starter questions (for 7–21 day window):
- What signals were most predictive of a failure?
- Which checks caught issues fastest? Which were noisy/low-signal?
- Did KV cache or batching behavior materially affect latency?
- Were communications timely and clear (internal + external)?
- What can be automated next time to reduce manual steps?

Release notes draft (bullet points — replace placeholders):
- New: Introduced traffic-shepherd routing option to enable incremental variant rollouts.
- Fix: Resolved a rare memory leak in the model-hosting shim that could surface under high-concurrency.
- Perf: Improved token-level throughput by ~8% on quantized Llama-variant (p95 latency improvement of ~25ms).
- Known issues: Small fraction of streaming sessions may see delayed end-of-stream markers during initial cache warmup. Observed ~0.05% of sessions.

Open questions / risks to resolve before final:
- Do we want to shorten per-step observation from 30m to 15m for non-critical regions? (tradeoff detection vs speed)
- Should the sample prompt set include production customer prompts for higher fidelity? (privacy review needed)
- Validate that rollback can be fully automated end-to-end (config + deployment) without human-in-loop for 3xx–5xx automated guardcases.

Appendix: quick command snippets and links
- Rollback CLI: infractl router set-weight --service api --variant v2 --weight 0.0 --region us-west1
- Canary inspect: telemetry query "service:api AND variant:v2 AND timeframe:15m"
- Manual QA checklist link: CON-4572/manual-qacases

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive on step sizes and thresholds; feedback welcome on tolerances per region.
- If approved, will convert this playbook into a templated runbook entry and attach to release templates in Confluence (CON-4572).

Drafted by: Maya Chen (release engineer)
Reviewed preliminary by: Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair
